**Transcription of the boxed text (letter by letter, as printed):**

قَالَ الْحَافِظُ ابْنُ حَجَرٍ رَحِمَهُ اللهُ: «. . . أَوْ بِتَغْيِيرٍ مَعَ بِقَاءِ السُّبَاقِ: فَالْمُصْحَفُ وَالْمُحْرَفُ».

**Answers to your checks:**

- **(a)** The word is **NOT السِّياق** (no شين, no ياء). Zooming in, the letter after the shadda is clearly a **ب** with a dot *below* and a damma on it: **السُّبَاقِ** (alef–lām–sīn–shadda+damma–bāʾ–alef–qāf). So it reads **بِقَاءِ السُّبَاقِ**, not بقاء السياق.
- **(b)** **Yes**, there is a colon (:) directly after السُّبَاقِ, before فَالْمُصْحَفُ.
- **(c)** The final words are printed exactly: **فَالْمُصْحَفُ وَالْمُحْرَفُ** (fāʾ–alif–lām–mīm–ṣād–ḥāʾ–fāʾ … wāw–alif–lām–mīm–ḥāʾ–rāʾ–fāʾ), fully vocalised as shown.

**Printed punctuation, exactly:**
- Colon (:) after رَحِمَهُ اللهُ
- Opening guillemet **«**
- The ellipsis is printed as **three separated dots**: «**. . .**»
- Closing guillemet **»**
- A final full stop (.) after the closing guillemet.

Nothing in the box appears unclear enough to require [؟] at this resolution, though the vowel on the ر of رَحِمَهُ is faint — it reads رَحِمَهُ.
